groups.title: Applicative foundation and irregular Sources
groups.proposal: Treat the applicative as a derivation that adds a participant tangential to the Source event. Let the user choose an inherent-applicative, irregular, or valence-neutral Source analysis only when that lexical or structural analysis is genuinely unsettled; derive object depth and participant consequences automatically from the typed Source.
groups.writingJob: Accept any open typed Source, preserve inherent applicative and irregular itzi or itta histories, support valence-neutral pairs, add the applicative participant, and derive the resulting object structure without using Canvas examples as a stem whitelist.
groups.readingJob: Explain the applicative participant relation, inherent applicatives, irregular Source histories, valence-neutral pairs, direct versus applicative object functions, and honorific-only observations through concise clickable cues.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended inherent, irregular, or valence-neutral Source analysis only where the final composition cannot derive it. The application derives mainline status, object depth, and all participant consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation, typed Source analysis, and participant controls; do not add controls for object count, mainline status, honorific notes, or listed example stems.

groups.title: Type-one applicatives
groups.proposal: Because Type 1 formation is lexically unpredictable, let the user select Type 1 for any open typed Source rather than choosing from a stem list. Replace the final Source vowel with iā, derive the shape changes and new participant automatically, and preserve a causative-versus-applicative choice only where the same form genuinely permits both.
groups.writingJob: Apply replacive iā to an open typed Source, delete its final vowel, derive licensed fusion and boundary changes, import the applicative participant, preserve all grammatically possible causative or applicative roles, and keep Canvas witnesses non-authoritative.
groups.readingJob: Show the Source boundary, removed vowel, iā, reconstructed formation, fusion, participant transfer, meanings, and causative-applicative ambiguity as reading guidance rather than admission criteria.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Type 1 because its lexical availability is not predictable and resolves Causative versus Applicative only when required for the intended composition. The application derives every regular form and participant consequence.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Applicative Type and a conditional derivation-role choice; do not add controls for deleted vowels, fusion, sound changes, example identity, or object depth.

groups.title: Type-two foundation and final-i Sources
groups.proposal: Let the user select Type 2 and its applicative participant, then use typed Source shape, class, and signed history to choose liā or huiā and derive final-i changes automatically. Ask for a Source-history choice only when more than one licensed history truly remains.
groups.writingJob: Derive liā or huiā from the open typed Source, attach liā to final-i Sources, apply vowel lengthening and the si-to-xi and tzi-or-ti-to-chi changes, preserve the silent āyi restriction, and convert a retained Source reflexive to shuntline ne.
groups.readingJob: Explain Type 2 structure, Source ending and history, suffix choice, automatic alternations, āyi restriction, reflexive-to-ne transfer, participant hierarchy, and Canvas examples with clickable cues.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Type 2 and the intended applicative participant or referent. A Source-history choice appears only when typed provenance does not already determine the route; the application derives suffix, alternations, reflexive transfer, and object levels.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Applicative Type, participant identity, and a conditional Source-history choice; do not add controls for liā versus huiā, vowel length, consonant alternations, ne, or object levels when the typed Source determines them.

groups.title: Final-a Source routes
groups.proposal: Derive the licensed final-a applicative route from Source shape and typed history, including recursive applicatives and regular vowel or consonant alternations; expose only a real Source-history or structural ambiguity.
groups.writingJob: Transform open final-a Sources through their licensed iā, liā, or huiā route, derive all regular segment changes, preserve recursive applicative structure, and calculate participant depth from the typed Source.
groups.readingJob: Show the Source ending, selected history, reconstructed boundary, automatic alternations, recursive link, participant structure, and example meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an unresolved licensed Source history or genuinely competing structure. The application derives the route, form changes, recursive depth, and participants.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source history and recursive derivation; do not add controls for predictable sound changes, suffix allomorphs, examples, or object levels.

groups.title: Shape- and class-based exceptions
groups.proposal: Apply the Canvas-authorized Class D, Class B iya or eya, and oya exception routes by Source class and shape, asking the user about transitivity or history only where the typed Source leaves a real question.
groups.writingJob: Derive exception behavior from typed Source class, ending, transitivity, and history for any matching open Source shape without restricting entry to listed examples.
groups.readingJob: Explain why each route departs from the neighboring pattern and show class, shape, transitivity, history, and witness evidence as guidance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user resolves only an unsettled oya transitivity or Source-history analysis. The application selects every route fixed by typed class and shape.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source Class, Valence, and conditional Source history; do not add a picker containing the Canvas stems.

groups.title: O-ā and huiā routes
groups.proposal: Use signed internal Source history to distinguish root-final l, root-final o, a-hui, i-hui, exception, and suppletive routes behind o-ā and huiā forms. Ask the user to choose a history only when provenance cannot recover it; never gate the rule by stem spelling.
groups.writingJob: Derive the licensed o-ā or huiā applicative from open typed Source shape and internal history, preserve fused, exceptional, and suppletive routes, and propagate the correct participant structure.
groups.readingJob: Show the hidden Source history, reconstructed formula, fusion, exception or suppletion, competing histories, participants, and example evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses among genuinely unresolved licensed internal histories. Signed prior derivation removes that choice; the application derives the form and participants.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse compact Source-history selection only when provenance is insufficient; do not add exact-stem rules or spelling-based authority.

groups.title: Special, parallel, and class behavior
groups.proposal: Preserve final-ō huiā ambiguity, rare tiā applicatives, parallel Type 1 and Type 2 formations, automatic Class C membership, and the basic participant transformation; expose only a real derivation-role, type, history, or imported-participant choice.
groups.writingJob: Build each licensed special or parallel applicative from the open typed Source, assign the Result to Class C, compact the Source, and import the new applicative object through the shared participant transformation.
groups.readingJob: Explain rare and parallel formations, causative-applicative homophony, Class C behavior, participant transfer, and example meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user resolves a genuine Type 1 versus Type 2, Causative versus Applicative, Source-history, or participant choice. The application derives class and transformation consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation Type, role, Source history, and participant controls; do not add a Class C or example control.

groups.title: Single-object applicative transformation
groups.proposal: Reuse the canonical applicative transformation for a Source without an existing object: the user supplies the new participant and genuine coreference, while the application derives the single applicative object and its form.
groups.writingJob: Compact the typed Source, import the applicative participant as specific, reflexive, or nonspecific, and derive all agreement and object realization from participant identity.
groups.readingJob: Show the Source-to-Result transformation, new participant, object realization, referent identity, and literal or lexical readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the new participant and resolves real coreference. The application derives the object form and participant structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse participant and identity controls; do not ask the user to choose object-pronoun shape or object level.

groups.title: Double-object applicatives and silent supplementation
groups.proposal: Build double-object applicatives from the typed transitive Source and participant identities, with mainline promotion, shuntline preservation, compatibility, silence, reflexive ne, and supplementation derived automatically.
groups.writingJob: Promote the applicative object to mainline, retain the Source object on the shuntline, enforce specific-object compatibility, derive silent realization and ne replacement, and authorize supplementation of any grammatically present silent object.
groups.readingJob: Show mainline and shuntline functions, participant identities, prefix order, silence, ne, supplement links, and example interpretations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the applicative participant, genuine referent identities, and a supplement head only if several eligible silent objects remain. The application derives hierarchy and realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse participant identity and Lesson 17 supplementation; do not expose manual mainline, shuntline, silence, ne, or prefix-order controls.

groups.title: Triple-object applicatives
groups.proposal: Recapture an eligible Result as the typed Source for another applicative layer and derive the mainline plus two shuntline levels through the normal recursive composition path.
groups.writingJob: Import the new applicative participant, preserve earlier objects and their functions, derive specificity, reflexivity, nonspecificity, silence, ne, compatibility, and prefix order without a separate triple-object engine.
groups.readingJob: Expose the recursive Source link, all three object levels, participant identities, silent realizations, incompatibilities, and example readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the recaptured Source, new participant, and genuine referent identity. The application derives ordering, levels, silence, ne, and compatibility.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse recursive composition and participant identity; do not add manual object-level, prefix-order, silence, or ne controls.

groups.title: Ambiguity, Mood, and Voice
groups.proposal: Preserve every licensed typed Source analysis for ambiguous applicatives and use the ordinary Mood and Voice owners on the completed Result. Ask the user to resolve a Source only for intended composition or real context, and to choose Mood or passive or impersonal Voice when desired.
groups.writingJob: Keep multiple Sources available, apply only grammatical ambiguity reducers, and feed the completed applicative through shared mood, passive, and impersonal transformations while retaining its participant hierarchy.
groups.readingJob: Show competing Sources, contextual readings, ambiguity reducers, Mood comparisons, Voice transformations, participant retention, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an intended Source only when composition or context requires it and chooses the intended Mood or Voice. The application preserves unresolved readings and derives all form and participant consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source analysis, Mood, and Voice; do not infer authority from the surface string or add Lesson-26-specific mood and voice controls.

groups.title: Object interpretation and applicative unit
groups.proposal: Preserve the licensed human and nonhuman object interpretations, deceptive surface ambiguity, and the close applicative-suffix/object unit. Let the user select an intended interpretation only when final composition or actual context requires it.
groups.writingJob: Derive all interpretations licensed by participant type and typed Source structure, preserve deceptive surface alternatives and causative-applicative closeness, and keep the applicative suffix linked to its imported object.
groups.readingJob: Show human or nonhuman interpretation, Source and Result roles, deceptive homophony, suffix-object linkage, causative comparison, contextual cues, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an intended participant interpretation or derivation role only where the grammar leaves a real alternative. The application derives all fixed readings and structural links.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse participant interpretation and conditional derivation-role choices; do not add controls for readings fixed by typed structure or for example stems.
